why: The inserted fallback to keep a marker together with a following dependent/clausal complement shifted the model's top-ranked cut choices (depth‑1 improved slightly but depth‑2 worsened notably), so the edit mainly changed the first one or two preferred cuts. That behavior helped examples where an adverbial or clause was kept with its head, but it also caused cuts to move into noun phrases, enumerations, and multiword names (e.g. splitting 'Cirque du Soleil' or 'assistance of 80 police'), producing balanced wins and losses and largest harm in the ≤5 bin.
lesson: Limit the fallback to true subordinating/clausal markers and avoid applying it when the 'marker' is part of an NP, named entity, or enumeration, because this change mainly alters top-ranked choices and will hurt short/medium-latency settings if it forces cuts inside multiword noun phrases.
